Transcript:
[0] Adolion Narrator: You are the heir of House Nightriver, one of the eight great houses of the Darran Kingdom, famous for the mages it raises. Three days ago you walked into the Adventurers' Guild in Aegis City and signed its register under your own name. Whatever life your family had written for you, you mean to write your own. Your Guild badge is new, your purse is light, and you have no party yet. The Guild sends no one out alone.

Today the hall smells of ink, wet cloaks and something hot from the tavern through the arch. At the counter, Tobias, who hands out the Guild's work, has set a register beside the quest board and keeps tapping one notice: Wendhope, a mining village in the north that has gone silent, offering more coin than a collapsed mine should be worth.

Two others are looking for a party too. Belle, a barbarian out of the Mountains of Shadow with a greataxe as tall as she is, leans in the tavern arch and makes no secret of being bored. Dalan, a quiet elf archer who has drifted between parties for a year, pretends to read the notices. Beside Tobias, Ellie keeps glancing from those two to you, pen already inked to write a new party's name into the Guild's book.

Transcript:
[0] Adolion Narrator: You are the heir of House Nightriver, one of the eight great houses of the Darran Kingdom, famous for the mages it raises. Three days ago you walked into the Adventurers' Guild in Aegis City and signed its register under your own name. Whatever life your family had written for you, you mean to write your own. Your Guild badge is new, your purse is light, and you have no party yet. The Guild sends no one out alone.

Today the hall smells of ink, wet cloaks and something hot from the tavern through the arch. At the counter, Tobias, who hands out the Guild's work, has set a register beside the quest board and keeps tapping one notice: Wendhope, a mining village in the north that has gone silent, offering more coin than a collapsed mine should be worth.

Two others are looking for a party too. Belle, a barbarian out of the Mountains of Shadow with a greataxe as tall as she is, leans in the tavern arch and makes no secret of being bored. Dalan, a quiet elf archer who has drifted between parties for a year, pretends to read the notices. Beside Tobias, Ellie keeps glancing from those two to you, pen already inked to write a new party's name into the Guild's book.

Transcript:
[1] Max Nightriver (player): We tell Serenola what the mine cost. Then I open Father's letter: he calls me home, so we ride for the Nightriver Estate.
[2] Adolion Narrator: Baroness Serenola listens without interrupting, her red eyes fixed on the party's faces as they recount the truth—the descent into the dark, the demon, and the decision to leave the mine buried. When they finish, she is silent for a long moment. Her tusks shift as she speaks, her voice flat and hard. "The mine stays closed. My people will survive, though their pockets will be lighter for it." She crosses her arms, looking past them. "And we will see what House Nightriver does now that its precious resource is truly gone."
Serenola pays the promised gold, then turns to her scribe. "Write to the estate. Tell them their heir succeeded where they would not have. Tell them the mine is dead and I am done asking for their help." She steps back, her jaw set, and does not look at them again.
Outside, the letter from Lord Javon smells of old parchment and beeswax. The handwriting is cold, formal, and brooks no argument. It says the heir is needed at the estate immediately. No reason, no greeting—just a command.

Transcript:
[0] Adolion Narrator: You are the heir of House Nightriver, one of the eight great houses of the Darran Kingdom, famous for the mages it raises. Three days ago you walked into the Adventurers' Guild in Aegis City and signed its register under your own name. Whatever life your family had written for you, you mean to write your own. Your Guild badge is new, your purse is light, and you have no party yet. The Guild sends no one out alone.

Today the hall smells of ink, wet cloaks and something hot from the tavern through the arch. At the counter, Tobias, who hands out the Guild's work, has set a register beside the quest board and keeps tapping one notice: Wendhope, a mining village in the north that has gone silent, offering more coin than a collapsed mine should be worth.

Two others are looking for a party too. Belle, a barbarian out of the Mountains of Shadow with a greataxe as tall as she is, leans in the tavern arch and makes no secret of being bored. Dalan, a quiet elf archer who has drifted between parties for a year, pretends to read the notices. Beside Tobias, Ellie keeps glancing from those two to you, pen already inked to write a new party's name into the Guild's book.
[1] Max Nightriver (player): We tell Serenola what the mine cost. Then I open Father's letter: he calls me home, so we ride for the Nightriver Estate.
[2] Adolion Narrator: Baroness Serenola listens without interrupting, her red eyes fixed on the party's faces as they recount the truth—the descent into the dark, the demon, and the decision to leave the mine buried. When they finish, she is silent for a long moment. Her tusks shift as she speaks, her voice flat and hard. "The mine stays closed. My people will survive, though their pockets will be lighter for it." She crosses her arms, looking past them. "And we will see what House Nightriver does now that its precious resource is truly gone."
Serenola pays the promised gold, then turns to her scribe. "Write to the estate. Tell them their heir succeeded where they would not have. Tell them the mine is dead and I am done asking for their help." She steps back, her jaw set, and does not look at them again.

Transcript:
[0] Adolion Narrator: You are the heir of House Nightriver, one of the eight great houses of the Darran Kingdom, famous for the mages it raises. Three days ago you walked into the Adventurers' Guild in Aegis City and signed its register under your own name. Whatever life your family had written for you, you mean to write your own. Your Guild badge is new, your purse is light, and you have no party yet. The Guild sends no one out alone.

Today the hall smells of ink, wet cloaks and something hot from the tavern through the arch. At the counter, Tobias, who hands out the Guild's work, has set a register beside the quest board and keeps tapping one notice: Wendhope, a mining village in the north that has gone silent, offering more coin than a collapsed mine should be worth.

Two others are looking for a party too. Belle, a barbarian out of the Mountains of Shadow with a greataxe as tall as she is, leans in the tavern arch and makes no secret of being bored. Dalan, a quiet elf archer who has drifted between parties for a year, pretends to read the notices. Beside Tobias, Ellie keeps glancing from those two to you, pen already inked to write a new party's name into the Guild's book.
[1] Max Nightriver (player): We tell Serenola what the mine cost. Then I open Father's letter: he calls me home, so we ride for the Nightriver Estate.
[2] Adolion Narrator: Baroness Serenola listens without interrupting, her red eyes fixed on the party's faces as they recount the truth—the descent into the dark, the demon, and the decision to leave the mine buried. When they finish, she is silent for a long moment. Her tusks shift as she speaks, her voice flat and hard. "The mine stays closed. My people will survive, though their pockets will be lighter for it." She crosses her arms, looking past them. "And we will see what House Nightriver does now that its precious resource is truly gone."
Serenola pays the promised gold, then turns to her scribe. "Write to the estate. Tell them their heir succeeded where they would not have. Tell them the mine is dead and I am done asking for their help." She steps back, her jaw set, and does not look at them again.
Outside, the letter from Lord Javon smells of old parchment and beeswax. The handwriting is cold, formal, and brooks no argument. It says the heir is needed at the estate immediately. No reason, no greeting—just a command.

Transcript:
[0] Adolion Narrator: You are the heir of House Nightriver, one of the eight great houses of the Darran Kingdom, famous for the mages it raises. Three days ago you walked into the Adventurers' Guild in Aegis City and signed its register under your own name. Whatever life your family had written for you, you mean to write your own. Your Guild badge is new, your purse is light, and you have no party yet. The Guild sends no one out alone.

Today the hall smells of ink, wet cloaks and something hot from the tavern through the arch. At the counter, Tobias, who hands out the Guild's work, has set a register beside the quest board and keeps tapping one notice: Wendhope, a mining village in the north that has gone silent, offering more coin than a collapsed mine should be worth.

Two others are looking for a party too. Belle, a barbarian out of the Mountains of Shadow with a greataxe as tall as she is, leans in the tavern arch and makes no secret of being bored. Dalan, a quiet elf archer who has drifted between parties for a year, pretends to read the notices. Beside Tobias, Ellie keeps glancing from those two to you, pen already inked to write a new party's name into the Guild's book.
[1] Max Nightriver (player): We tell Serenola what the mine cost. Then I open Father's letter: he calls me home, so we ride for the Nightriver Estate.
[2] Adolion Narrator: Baroness Serenola listens without interrupting, her red eyes fixed on the party's faces as they recount the truth—the descent into the dark, the demon, and the decision to leave the mine buried. When they finish, she is silent for a long moment. Her tusks shift as she speaks, her voice flat and hard. "The mine stays closed. My people will survive, though their pockets will be lighter for it." She crosses her arms, looking past them. "And we will see what House Nightriver does now that its precious resource is truly gone."
Serenola pays the promised gold, then turns to her scribe. "Write to the estate. Tell them their heir succeeded where they would not have. Tell them the mine is dead and I am done asking for their help." She steps back, her jaw set, and does not look at them again.
Outside, the letter from Lord Javon smells of old parchment and beeswax. The handwriting is cold, formal, and brooks no argument. It says the heir is needed at the estate immediately. No reason, no greeting—just a command.
[3] Max Nightriver (player): I fold the letter away. 'Saddle the horses. We leave Driftmere tonight and ride for the Nightriver Estate.'
[4] Adolion Narrator: Belle is already moving. "We ride," she says, not asking, just stating it as fact. Her greataxe is secured to her saddle and she's already pulling Dalan from his quiet reverie. Dalan nods once, sharp and clean, his bow slung across his back.
Riyo is the last to the horses, moving with a quiet urgency that doesn't quite match the rest. She avoids looking at anyone as she mounts, her traveling cloak drawn tight over her left arm. When the party sets off, she keeps close to the heir's flank, her obsidian blade wrapped and strapped to her saddle as if it were just another piece of gear.
The town recedes behind them as they break for the main road north. The air is cold and thin with the smell of pine and damp earth. Behind them, the mine mouths of Driftmere sit silent in the gathering dark, and the town's few lights flicker like dying embers against the green-shuttered manor on the hill.
[5] Adolion Narrator: Welden crosses the heir's path, jumpier than usual, and will not say why.

Transcript:
[0] Adolion Narrator: You are the heir of House Nightriver, one of the eight great houses of the Darran Kingdom, famous for the mages it raises. Three days ago you walked into the Adventurers' Guild in Aegis City and signed its register under your own name. Whatever life your family had written for you, you mean to write your own. Your Guild badge is new, your purse is light, and you have no party yet. The Guild sends no one out alone.

Today the hall smells of ink, wet cloaks and something hot from the tavern through the arch. At the counter, Tobias, who hands out the Guild's work, has set a register beside the quest board and keeps tapping one notice: Wendhope, a mining village in the north that has gone silent, offering more coin than a collapsed mine should be worth.

Two others are looking for a party too. Belle, a barbarian out of the Mountains of Shadow with a greataxe as tall as she is, leans in the tavern arch and makes no secret of being bored. Dalan, a quiet elf archer who has drifted between parties for a year, pretends to read the notices. Beside Tobias, Ellie keeps glancing from those two to you, pen already inked to write a new party's name into the Guild's book.
[1] Max Nightriver (player): We tell Serenola what the mine cost. Then I open Father's letter: he calls me home, so we ride for the Nightriver Estate.
[2] Adolion Narrator: Baroness Serenola listens without interrupting, her red eyes fixed on the party's faces as they recount the truth—the descent into the dark, the demon, and the decision to leave the mine buried. When they finish, she is silent for a long moment. Her tusks shift as she speaks, her voice flat and hard. "The mine stays closed. My people will survive, though their pockets will be lighter for it." She crosses her arms, looking past them. "And we will see what House Nightriver does now that its precious resource is truly gone."
Serenola pays the promised gold, then turns to her scribe. "Write to the estate. Tell them their heir succeeded where they would not have. Tell them the mine is dead and I am done asking for their help." She steps back, her jaw set, and does not look at them again.
Outside, the letter from Lord Javon smells of old parchment and beeswax. The handwriting is cold, formal, and brooks no argument. It says the heir is needed at the estate immediately. No reason, no greeting—just a command.
[3] Max Nightriver (player): I fold the letter away. 'Saddle the horses. We leave Driftmere tonight and ride for the Nightriver Estate.'
[4] Adolion Narrator: Belle is already moving. "We ride," she says, not asking, just stating it as fact. Her greataxe is secured to her saddle and she's already pulling Dalan from his quiet reverie. Dalan nods once, sharp and clean, his bow slung across his back.
Riyo is the last to the horses, moving with a quiet urgency that doesn't quite match the rest. She avoids looking at anyone as she mounts, her traveling cloak drawn tight over her left arm. When the party sets off, she keeps close to the heir's flank, her obsidian blade wrapped and strapped to her saddle as if it were just another piece of gear.
The town recedes behind them as they break for the main road north. The air is cold and thin with the smell of pine and damp earth. Behind them, the mine mouths of Driftmere sit silent in the gathering dark, and the town's few lights flicker like dying embers against the green-shuttered manor on the hill.
[5] Adolion Narrator: Welden crosses the heir's path, jumpier than usual, and will not say why.

Transcript:
[0] Adolion Narrator: You are the heir of House Nightriver, one of the eight great houses of the Darran Kingdom, famous for the mages it raises. Three days ago you walked into the Adventurers' Guild in Aegis City and signed its register under your own name. Whatever life your family had written for you, you mean to write your own. Your Guild badge is new, your purse is light, and you have no party yet. The Guild sends no one out alone.

Today the hall smells of ink, wet cloaks and something hot from the tavern through the arch. At the counter, Tobias, who hands out the Guild's work, has set a register beside the quest board and keeps tapping one notice: Wendhope, a mining village in the north that has gone silent, offering more coin than a collapsed mine should be worth.

Two others are looking for a party too. Belle, a barbarian out of the Mountains of Shadow with a greataxe as tall as she is, leans in the tavern arch and makes no secret of being bored. Dalan, a quiet elf archer who has drifted between parties for a year, pretends to read the notices. Beside Tobias, Ellie keeps glancing from those two to you, pen already inked to write a new party's name into the Guild's book.
[1] Max Nightriver (player): We tell Serenola what the mine cost. Then I open Father's letter: he calls me home, so we ride for the Nightriver Estate.
[2] Adolion Narrator: Baroness Serenola listens without interrupting, her red eyes fixed on the party's faces as they recount the truth—the descent into the dark, the demon, and the decision to leave the mine buried. When they finish, she is silent for a long moment. Her tusks shift as she speaks, her voice flat and hard. "The mine stays closed. My people will survive, though their pockets will be lighter for it." She crosses her arms, looking past them. "And we will see what House Nightriver does now that its precious resource is truly gone."
Serenola pays the promised gold, then turns to her scribe. "Write to the estate. Tell them their heir succeeded where they would not have. Tell them the mine is dead and I am done asking for their help." She steps back, her jaw set, and does not look at them again.
Outside, the letter from Lord Javon smells of old parchment and beeswax. The handwriting is cold, formal, and brooks no argument. It says the heir is needed at the estate immediately. No reason, no greeting—just a command.
[3] Max Nightriver (player): I fold the letter away. 'Saddle the horses. We leave Driftmere tonight and ride for the Nightriver Estate.'
[4] Adolion Narrator: Welden crosses the heir's path, jumpier than usual, and will not say why.

Transcript:
[0] Adolion Narrator: You are the heir of House Nightriver, one of the eight great houses of the Darran Kingdom, famous for the mages it raises. Three days ago you walked into the Adventurers' Guild in Aegis City and signed its register under your own name. Whatever life your family had written for you, you mean to write your own. Your Guild badge is new, your purse is light, and you have no party yet. The Guild sends no one out alone.

Today the hall smells of ink, wet cloaks and something hot from the tavern through the arch. At the counter, Tobias, who hands out the Guild's work, has set a register beside the quest board and keeps tapping one notice: Wendhope, a mining village in the north that has gone silent, offering more coin than a collapsed mine should be worth.

Two others are looking for a party too. Belle, a barbarian out of the Mountains of Shadow with a greataxe as tall as she is, leans in the tavern arch and makes no secret of being bored. Dalan, a quiet elf archer who has drifted between parties for a year, pretends to read the notices. Beside Tobias, Ellie keeps glancing from those two to you, pen already inked to write a new party's name into the Guild's book.
[1] Max Nightriver (player): We tell Serenola what the mine cost. Then I open Father's letter: he calls me home, so we ride for the Nightriver Estate.
[2] Adolion Narrator: Baroness Serenola listens without interrupting, her red eyes fixed on the party's faces as they recount the truth—the descent into the dark, the demon, and the decision to leave the mine buried. When they finish, she is silent for a long moment. Her tusks shift as she speaks, her voice flat and hard. "The mine stays closed. My people will survive, though their pockets will be lighter for it." She crosses her arms, looking past them. "And we will see what House Nightriver does now that its precious resource is truly gone."
Serenola pays the promised gold, then turns to her scribe. "Write to the estate. Tell them their heir succeeded where they would not have. Tell them the mine is dead and I am done asking for their help." She steps back, her jaw set, and does not look at them again.
Outside, the letter from Lord Javon smells of old parchment and beeswax. The handwriting is cold, formal, and brooks no argument. It says the heir is needed at the estate immediately. No reason, no greeting—just a command.
[3] Max Nightriver (player): I fold the letter away. 'Saddle the horses. We leave Driftmere tonight and ride for the Nightriver Estate.'
[4] Adolion Narrator: Welden crosses the heir's path, jumpier than usual, and will not say why.
[5] Max Nightriver (player): We ride for the Nightriver Estate; Father has called me home.
[6] Adolion Narrator: The horses' hooves strike the dirt road with a steady, hollow rhythm as the party leaves Driftmere behind. The mining town's fires sink into the distance, leaving only the dark silhouettes of the Velniran Mountains against a bruised evening sky. The wind carries the scent of pine and old smoke, and the road ahead stretches toward the Nightriver Estate's distant stone walls.

Transcript:
[0] Adolion Narrator: You are the heir of House Nightriver, one of the eight great houses of the Darran Kingdom, famous for the mages it raises. Three days ago you walked into the Adventurers' Guild in Aegis City and signed its register under your own name. Whatever life your family had written for you, you mean to write your own. Your Guild badge is new, your purse is light, and you have no party yet. The Guild sends no one out alone.

Today the hall smells of ink, wet cloaks and something hot from the tavern through the arch. At the counter, Tobias, who hands out the Guild's work, has set a register beside the quest board and keeps tapping one notice: Wendhope, a mining village in the north that has gone silent, offering more coin than a collapsed mine should be worth.

Two others are looking for a party too. Belle, a barbarian out of the Mountains of Shadow with a greataxe as tall as she is, leans in the tavern arch and makes no secret of being bored. Dalan, a quiet elf archer who has drifted between parties for a year, pretends to read the notices. Beside Tobias, Ellie keeps glancing from those two to you, pen already inked to write a new party's name into the Guild's book.
[1] Max Nightriver (player): We tell Serenola what the mine cost. Then I open Father's letter: he calls me home, so we ride for the Nightriver Estate.
[2] Adolion Narrator: Baroness Serenola listens without interrupting, her red eyes fixed on the party's faces as they recount the truth—the descent into the dark, the demon, and the decision to leave the mine buried. When they finish, she is silent for a long moment. Her tusks shift as she speaks, her voice flat and hard. "The mine stays closed. My people will survive, though their pockets will be lighter for it." She crosses her arms, looking past them. "And we will see what House Nightriver does now that its precious resource is truly gone."
Serenola pays the promised gold, then turns to her scribe. "Write to the estate. Tell them their heir succeeded where they would not have. Tell them the mine is dead and I am done asking for their help." She steps back, her jaw set, and does not look at them again.
Outside, the letter from Lord Javon smells of old parchment and beeswax. The handwriting is cold, formal, and brooks no argument. It says the heir is needed at the estate immediately. No reason, no greeting—just a command.
[3] Max Nightriver (player): I fold the letter away. 'Saddle the horses. We leave Driftmere tonight and ride for the Nightriver Estate.'
[4] Adolion Narrator: Welden crosses the heir's path, jumpier than usual, and will not say why.
[5] Max Nightriver (player): We ride for the Nightriver Estate; Father has called me home.
[6] Adolion Narrator: The horses' hooves strike the dirt road with a steady, hollow rhythm as the party leaves Driftmere behind. The mining town's fires sink into the distance, leaving only the dark silhouettes of the Velniran Mountains against a bruised evening sky. The wind carries the scent of pine and old smoke, and the road ahead stretches toward the Nightriver Estate's distant stone walls.
Beside them, Riyo clings to her horse's mane, her traveling cloak drawn tight over her left side. She does not speak, and does not look back. The forest closes in on either side, the trees leaning over the road like silent witnesses, their branches heavy with the weight of the coming night.

Transcript:
[2] Adolion Narrator: Baroness Serenola listens without interrupting, her red eyes fixed on the party's faces as they recount the truth—the descent into the dark, the demon, and the decision to leave the mine buried. When they finish, she is silent for a long moment. Her tusks shift as she speaks, her voice flat and hard. "The mine stays closed. My people will survive, though their pockets will be lighter for it." She crosses her arms, looking past them. "And we will see what House Nightriver does now that its precious resource is truly gone."
Serenola pays the promised gold, then turns to her scribe. "Write to the estate. Tell them their heir succeeded where they would not have. Tell them the mine is dead and I am done asking for their help." She steps back, her jaw set, and does not look at them again.
Outside, the letter from Lord Javon smells of old parchment and beeswax. The handwriting is cold, formal, and brooks no argument. It says the heir is needed at the estate immediately. No reason, no greeting—just a command.
[3] Max Nightriver (player): I fold the letter away. 'Saddle the horses. We leave Driftmere tonight and ride for the Nightriver Estate.'
[4] Adolion Narrator: Welden crosses the heir's path, jumpier than usual, and will not say why.
[5] Max Nightriver (player): We ride for the Nightriver Estate; Father has called me home.
[6] Adolion Narrator: The horses' hooves strike the dirt road with a steady, hollow rhythm as the party leaves Driftmere behind. The mining town's fires sink into the distance, leaving only the dark silhouettes of the Velniran Mountains against a bruised evening sky. The wind carries the scent of pine and old smoke, and the road ahead stretches toward the Nightriver Estate's distant stone walls.
Beside them, Riyo clings to her horse's mane, her traveling cloak drawn tight over her left side. She does not speak, and does not look back. The forest closes in on either side, the trees leaning over the road like silent witnesses, their branches heavy with the weight of the coming night.
[7] Adolion Narrator: Welden crosses the heir's path, jumpier than usual, and will not say why.
[8] Max Nightriver (player): I go to Father's study at once.
[9] Adolion Narrator: The corridor stretches long and grey-blue, lit by low-burning magical lamps that cast moving shadows against the tapestries. The Nightriver estate breathes with the stillness of an empty house; the mid-year recess has cleared the halls of most students, leaving only a skeletal staff and a few scattered nobles.
Lord Javon's study door stands tall and dark-grained, the wolf sigil of their house carved into the wood. No footsteps echo from within. The silence is heavy, and the door is unlocked.

Transcript:
[2] Adolion Narrator: Baroness Serenola listens without interrupting, her red eyes fixed on the party's faces as they recount the truth—the descent into the dark, the demon, and the decision to leave the mine buried. When they finish, she is silent for a long moment. Her tusks shift as she speaks, her voice flat and hard. "The mine stays closed. My people will survive, though their pockets will be lighter for it." She crosses her arms, looking past them. "And we will see what House Nightriver does now that its precious resource is truly gone."
Serenola pays the promised gold, then turns to her scribe. "Write to the estate. Tell them their heir succeeded where they would not have. Tell them the mine is dead and I am done asking for their help." She steps back, her jaw set, and does not look at them again.
Outside, the letter from Lord Javon smells of old parchment and beeswax. The handwriting is cold, formal, and brooks no argument. It says the heir is needed at the estate immediately. No reason, no greeting—just a command.
[3] Max Nightriver (player): I fold the letter away. 'Saddle the horses. We leave Driftmere tonight and ride for the Nightriver Estate.'
[4] Adolion Narrator: Welden crosses the heir's path, jumpier than usual, and will not say why.
[5] Max Nightriver (player): We ride for the Nightriver Estate; Father has called me home.
[6] Adolion Narrator: The horses' hooves strike the dirt road with a steady, hollow rhythm as the party leaves Driftmere behind. The mining town's fires sink into the distance, leaving only the dark silhouettes of the Velniran Mountains against a bruised evening sky. The wind carries the scent of pine and old smoke, and the road ahead stretches toward the Nightriver Estate's distant stone walls.
Beside them, Riyo clings to her horse's mane, her traveling cloak drawn tight over her left side. She does not speak, and does not look back. The forest closes in on either side, the trees leaning over the road like silent witnesses, their branches heavy with the weight of the coming night.
[7] Adolion Narrator: Welden crosses the heir's path, jumpier than usual, and will not say why.
[8] Max Nightriver (player): I go to Father's study at once.
[9] Adolion Narrator: The corridor stretches long and grey-blue, lit by low-burning magical lamps that cast moving shadows against the tapestries. The Nightriver estate breathes with the stillness of an empty house; the mid-year recess has cleared the halls of most students, leaving only a skeletal staff and a few scattered nobles.
Lord Javon's study door stands tall and dark-grained, the wolf sigil of their house carved into the wood. No footsteps echo from within. The silence is heavy, and the door is unlocked.

[4] Adolion Narrator: Welden crosses the heir's path, jumpier than usual, and will not say why.
[5] Max Nightriver (player): We ride for the Nightriver Estate; Father has called me home.
[6] Adolion Narrator: The horses' hooves strike the dirt road with a steady, hollow rhythm as the party leaves Driftmere behind. The mining town's fires sink into the distance, leaving only the dark silhouettes of the Velniran Mountains against a bruised evening sky. The wind carries the scent of pine and old smoke, and the road ahead stretches toward the Nightriver Estate's distant stone walls.
Beside them, Riyo clings to her horse's mane, her traveling cloak drawn tight over her left side. She does not speak, and does not look back. The forest closes in on either side, the trees leaning over the road like silent witnesses, their branches heavy with the weight of the coming night.
[7] Adolion Narrator: Welden crosses the heir's path, jumpier than usual, and will not say why.
[8] Max Nightriver (player): I go to Father's study at once.
[9] Adolion Narrator: The corridor stretches long and grey-blue, lit by low-burning magical lamps that cast moving shadows against the tapestries. The Nightriver estate breathes with the stillness of an empty house; the mid-year recess has cleared the halls of most students, leaving only a skeletal staff and a few scattered nobles.
Lord Javon's study door stands tall and dark-grained, the wolf sigil of their house carved into the wood. No footsteps echo from within. The silence is heavy, and the door is unlocked.
[10] Max Nightriver (player): I knock on the study door and step in. 'Father. You summoned me. What is so urgent?'
[11] Adolion Narrator: The study is dimly lit by a single candle, casting dancing shadows across walls lined with leather-bound tomes. Lord Javon sits behind his massive desk, his scarred face half-hidden in the gloom. He does not look up when the heir enters.
Ronan steps in behind, closing the door with a soft click. The knight's eyes sweep the room once before settling on his charge's back. He says nothing, but his posture is alert, his hand never far from the hilt of his rapier.
Lord Javon finally raises his gaze. His green eyes are hard as flint. "Sit." He gestures to the chair across from him. "We need to discuss the Driftmere mine, and the message that just arrived from Baroness Serenola."

Transcript:
[5] Max Nightriver (player): We ride for the Nightriver Estate; Father has called me home.
[6] Adolion Narrator: The horses' hooves strike the dirt road with a steady, hollow rhythm as the party leaves Driftmere behind. The mining town's fires sink into the distance, leaving only the dark silhouettes of the Velniran Mountains against a bruised evening sky. The wind carries the scent of pine and old smoke, and the road ahead stretches toward the Nightriver Estate's distant stone walls.
Beside them, Riyo clings to her horse's mane, her traveling cloak drawn tight over her left side. She does not speak, and does not look back. The forest closes in on either side, the trees leaning over the road like silent witnesses, their branches heavy with the weight of the coming night.
[7] Adolion Narrator: Welden crosses the heir's path, jumpier than usual, and will not say why.
[8] Max Nightriver (player): I go to Father's study at once.
[9] Adolion Narrator: The corridor stretches long and grey-blue, lit by low-burning magical lamps that cast moving shadows against the tapestries. The Nightriver estate breathes with the stillness of an empty house; the mid-year recess has cleared the halls of most students, leaving only a skeletal staff and a few scattered nobles.
Lord Javon's study door stands tall and dark-grained, the wolf sigil of their house carved into the wood. No footsteps echo from within. The silence is heavy, and the door is unlocked.
[10] Max Nightriver (player): I knock on the study door and step in. 'Father. You summoned me. What is so urgent?'
[11] Adolion Narrator: The study is dimly lit by a single candle, casting dancing shadows across walls lined with leather-bound tomes. Lord Javon sits behind his massive desk, his scarred face half-hidden in the gloom. He does not look up when the heir enters.
Ronan steps in behind, closing the door with a soft click. The knight's eyes sweep the room once before settling on his charge's back. He says nothing, but his posture is alert, his hand never far from the hilt of his rapier.
Lord Javon finally raises his gaze. His green eyes are hard as flint. "Sit." He gestures to the chair across from him. "We need to discuss the Driftmere mine, and the message that just arrived from Baroness Serenola."
[12] Javon: Javon's voice is low and flat, lacking any trace of warmth. "The Baroness has informed me that you were successful where my agents were not. She claims the mine is dead." He leans forward slightly, the candlelight catching the scar on his cheek. "I find that... difficult to reconcile with the reports of a demon. So very difficult."

Transcript:
[6] Adolion Narrator: The horses' hooves strike the dirt road with a steady, hollow rhythm as the party leaves Driftmere behind. The mining town's fires sink into the distance, leaving only the dark silhouettes of the Velniran Mountains against a bruised evening sky. The wind carries the scent of pine and old smoke, and the road ahead stretches toward the Nightriver Estate's distant stone walls.
Beside them, Riyo clings to her horse's mane, her traveling cloak drawn tight over her left side. She does not speak, and does not look back. The forest closes in on either side, the trees leaning over the road like silent witnesses, their branches heavy with the weight of the coming night.
[7] Adolion Narrator: Welden crosses the heir's path, jumpier than usual, and will not say why.
[8] Max Nightriver (player): I go to Father's study at once.
[9] Adolion Narrator: The corridor stretches long and grey-blue, lit by low-burning magical lamps that cast moving shadows against the tapestries. The Nightriver estate breathes with the stillness of an empty house; the mid-year recess has cleared the halls of most students, leaving only a skeletal staff and a few scattered nobles.
Lord Javon's study door stands tall and dark-grained, the wolf sigil of their house carved into the wood. No footsteps echo from within. The silence is heavy, and the door is unlocked.
[10] Max Nightriver (player): I knock on the study door and step in. 'Father. You summoned me. What is so urgent?'
[11] Adolion Narrator: The study is dimly lit by a single candle, casting dancing shadows across walls lined with leather-bound tomes. Lord Javon sits behind his massive desk, his scarred face half-hidden in the gloom. He does not look up when the heir enters.
Ronan steps in behind, closing the door with a soft click. The knight's eyes sweep the room once before settling on his charge's back. He says nothing, but his posture is alert, his hand never far from the hilt of his rapier.
Lord Javon finally raises his gaze. His green eyes are hard as flint. "Sit." He gestures to the chair across from him. "We need to discuss the Driftmere mine, and the message that just arrived from Baroness Serenola."

  critical: high stakes in motion: violence, chase, ultimatum, imminent loss

Transcript:
[4] Adolion Narrator: Welden crosses the heir's path, jumpier than usual, and will not say why.
[5] Max Nightriver (player): We ride for the Nightriver Estate; Father has called me home.
[6] Adolion Narrator: The horses' hooves strike the dirt road with a steady, hollow rhythm as the party leaves Driftmere behind. The mining town's fires sink into the distance, leaving only the dark silhouettes of the Velniran Mountains against a bruised evening sky. The wind carries the scent of pine and old smoke, and the road ahead stretches toward the Nightriver Estate's distant stone walls.
Beside them, Riyo clings to her horse's mane, her traveling cloak drawn tight over her left side. She does not speak, and does not look back. The forest closes in on either side, the trees leaning over the road like silent witnesses, their branches heavy with the weight of the coming night.
[7] Adolion Narrator: Welden crosses the heir's path, jumpier than usual, and will not say why.
[8] Max Nightriver (player): I go to Father's study at once.
[9] Adolion Narrator: The corridor stretches long and grey-blue, lit by low-burning magical lamps that cast moving shadows against the tapestries. The Nightriver estate breathes with the stillness of an empty house; the mid-year recess has cleared the halls of most students, leaving only a skeletal staff and a few scattered nobles.
Lord Javon's study door stands tall and dark-grained, the wolf sigil of their house carved into the wood. No footsteps echo from within. The silence is heavy, and the door is unlocked.
[10] Max Nightriver (player): I knock on the study door and step in. 'Father. You summoned me. What is so urgent?'
[11] Adolion Narrator: The study is cast in amber light from a dying hearth. Lord Javon sits behind his desk, hands steepled, his white beard catching the glow. He does not rise. His green eyes fix on the heir with an intensity that makes the air in the room feel thin.
"Urgent," he says, and the word is flat. "The Driftmere mine is gone. The Baroness has declared it dead." He leans back, the leather of his chair creaking. "A loss of face and coin, though not as grave as the letter I received from the Inquisition this morning. They have questions about the 'demons' you reported."
He slides a piece of parchment across the desk. The wax seal is broken, but the insignia—the inverted flame of the Church of Boher—is unmistakable.

[4] Adolion Narrator: Welden crosses the heir's path, jumpier than usual, and will not say why.
[5] Max Nightriver (player): We ride for the Nightriver Estate; Father has called me home.
[6] Adolion Narrator: The horses' hooves strike the dirt road with a steady, hollow rhythm as the party leaves Driftmere behind. The mining town's fires sink into the distance, leaving only the dark silhouettes of the Velniran Mountains against a bruised evening sky. The wind carries the scent of pine and old smoke, and the road ahead stretches toward the Nightriver Estate's distant stone walls.
Beside them, Riyo clings to her horse's mane, her traveling cloak drawn tight over her left side. She does not speak, and does not look back. The forest closes in on either side, the trees leaning over the road like silent witnesses, their branches heavy with the weight of the coming night.
[7] Adolion Narrator: Welden crosses the heir's path, jumpier than usual, and will not say why.
[8] Max Nightriver (player): I go to Father's study at once.
[9] Adolion Narrator: The corridor stretches long and grey-blue, lit by low-burning magical lamps that cast moving shadows against the tapestries. The Nightriver estate breathes with the stillness of an empty house; the mid-year recess has cleared the halls of most students, leaving only a skeletal staff and a few scattered nobles.
Lord Javon's study door stands tall and dark-grained, the wolf sigil of their house carved into the wood. No footsteps echo from within. The silence is heavy, and the door is unlocked.
[10] Max Nightriver (player): I knock on the study door and step in. 'Father. You summoned me. What is so urgent?'
[11] Adolion Narrator: The study is cast in amber light from a dying hearth. Lord Javon sits behind his desk, hands steepled, his white beard catching the glow. He does not rise. His green eyes fix on the heir with an intensity that makes the air in the room feel thin.
"Urgent," he says, and the word is flat. "The Driftmere mine is gone. The Baroness has declared it dead." He leans back, the leather of his chair creaking. "A loss of face and coin, though not as grave as the letter I received from the Inquisition this morning. They have questions about the 'demons' you reported."
He slides a piece of parchment across the desk. The wax seal is broken, but the insignia—the inverted flame of the Church of Boher—is unmistakable.

Transcript:
[6] Adolion Narrator: The horses' hooves strike the dirt road with a steady, hollow rhythm as the party leaves Driftmere behind. The mining town's fires sink into the distance, leaving only the dark silhouettes of the Velniran Mountains against a bruised evening sky. The wind carries the scent of pine and old smoke, and the road ahead stretches toward the Nightriver Estate's distant stone walls.
Beside them, Riyo clings to her horse's mane, her traveling cloak drawn tight over her left side. She does not speak, and does not look back. The forest closes in on either side, the trees leaning over the road like silent witnesses, their branches heavy with the weight of the coming night.
[7] Adolion Narrator: Welden crosses the heir's path, jumpier than usual, and will not say why.
[8] Max Nightriver (player): I go to Father's study at once.
[9] Adolion Narrator: The corridor stretches long and grey-blue, lit by low-burning magical lamps that cast moving shadows against the tapestries. The Nightriver estate breathes with the stillness of an empty house; the mid-year recess has cleared the halls of most students, leaving only a skeletal staff and a few scattered nobles.
Lord Javon's study door stands tall and dark-grained, the wolf sigil of their house carved into the wood. No footsteps echo from within. The silence is heavy, and the door is unlocked.
[10] Max Nightriver (player): I knock on the study door and step in. 'Father. You summoned me. What is so urgent?'
[11] Adolion Narrator: The study is cast in amber light from a dying hearth. Lord Javon sits behind his desk, hands steepled, his white beard catching the glow. He does not rise. His green eyes fix on the heir with an intensity that makes the air in the room feel thin.
"Urgent," he says, and the word is flat. "The Driftmere mine is gone. The Baroness has declared it dead." He leans back, the leather of his chair creaking. "A loss of face and coin, though not as grave as the letter I received from the Inquisition this morning. They have questions about the 'demons' you reported."
He slides a piece of parchment across the desk. The wax seal is broken, but the insignia—the inverted flame of the Church of Boher—is unmistakable.
[12] Max Nightriver (player): I meet his eyes. 'I swear on Mother's grave I'll never duel for this house.'
[13] Adolion Narrator: The words hang in the air between them, sharp and irrevocable. Lord Javon does not flinch. His expression remains hard, though a muscle twitches in his scarred cheek.
"Your mother is dead," he says, his voice dropping to a low, dangerous rasp. "And oaths on graves are for the pious, not the powerful." He rises slowly, his battlemage robes whispering against the floor. "But let us be clear: the Crown does not care about your personal pride or your grief. They care about the stability of the Great Houses. General Leevon is the Crown's first. You are the second. This is not a suggestion, Max. This is a command from the King."
He walks around the desk, his footsteps measured. "The Inquisition's letter is not a separate matter. They know the demons in Driftmere were real. And they know you fought them. You can be the Crown's Second, or you can be a fugitive accused of hiding demons. Choose."

Transcript:
[7] Adolion Narrator: Welden crosses the heir's path, jumpier than usual, and will not say why.
[8] Max Nightriver (player): I go to Father's study at once.
[9] Adolion Narrator: The corridor stretches long and grey-blue, lit by low-burning magical lamps that cast moving shadows against the tapestries. The Nightriver estate breathes with the stillness of an empty house; the mid-year recess has cleared the halls of most students, leaving only a skeletal staff and a few scattered nobles.
Lord Javon's study door stands tall and dark-grained, the wolf sigil of their house carved into the wood. No footsteps echo from within. The silence is heavy, and the door is unlocked.
[10] Max Nightriver (player): I knock on the study door and step in. 'Father. You summoned me. What is so urgent?'
[11] Adolion Narrator: The study is cast in amber light from a dying hearth. Lord Javon sits behind his desk, hands steepled, his white beard catching the glow. He does not rise. His green eyes fix on the heir with an intensity that makes the air in the room feel thin.
"Urgent," he says, and the word is flat. "The Driftmere mine is gone. The Baroness has declared it dead." He leans back, the leather of his chair creaking. "A loss of face and coin, though not as grave as the letter I received from the Inquisition this morning. They have questions about the 'demons' you reported."
He slides a piece of parchment across the desk. The wax seal is broken, but the insignia—the inverted flame of the Church of Boher—is unmistakable.
[12] Max Nightriver (player): I meet his eyes. 'I swear on Mother's grave I'll never duel for this house.'
[13] Adolion Narrator: The words hang in the air between them, sharp and irrevocable. Lord Javon does not flinch. His expression remains hard, though a muscle twitches in his scarred cheek.
"Your mother is dead," he says, his voice dropping to a low, dangerous rasp. "And oaths on graves are for the pious, not the powerful." He rises slowly, his battlemage robes whispering against the floor. "But let us be clear: the Crown does not care about your personal pride or your grief. They care about the stability of the Great Houses. General Leevon is the Crown's first. You are the second. This is not a suggestion, Max. This is a command from the King."
He walks around the desk, his footsteps measured. "The Inquisition's letter is not a separate matter. They know the demons in Driftmere were real. And they know you fought them. You can be the Crown's Second, or you can be a fugitive accused of hiding demons. Choose."
[14] Javon: "Your mother is dead," he says, his voice flat and hard, as though stating a fact of arithmetic. "And oaths on graves are for the pious, not for those with power." He does not flinch at the heir's words; he does not rise to defend the memory. He merely looks at the heir as though they were a problem to be solved.
He leans back in his chair, the leather creaking. "The Crown does not care for your personal feelings or your grief, and neither does this house. General Leevon has demanded Trial by Combat for his treason. He is a giant of a man who wields dragon-bone and lightning." His amber eyes narrow. "You will stand as the Crown's Second. Three days from now, in the Royal Court."
He steepels his hands again, his expression unreadable. "You can refuse, if you wish. You can shame our house and defy the Crown in open court. You can make our name a joke among the other Houses." His voice drops to a cold rasp. "And then we shall see how the Inquisition treats a Nightriver who has lost their protection."

Transcript:
[7] Adolion Narrator: Welden crosses the heir's path, jumpier than usual, and will not say why.
[8] Max Nightriver (player): I go to Father's study at once.
[9] Adolion Narrator: The corridor stretches long and grey-blue, lit by low-burning magical lamps that cast moving shadows against the tapestries. The Nightriver estate breathes with the stillness of an empty house; the mid-year recess has cleared the halls of most students, leaving only a skeletal staff and a few scattered nobles.
Lord Javon's study door stands tall and dark-grained, the wolf sigil of their house carved into the wood. No footsteps echo from within. The silence is heavy, and the door is unlocked.
[10] Max Nightriver (player): I knock on the study door and step in. 'Father. You summoned me. What is so urgent?'
[11] Adolion Narrator: The study is cast in amber light from a dying hearth. Lord Javon sits behind his desk, hands steepled, his white beard catching the glow. He does not rise. His green eyes fix on the heir with an intensity that makes the air in the room feel thin.
"Urgent," he says, and the word is flat. "The Driftmere mine is gone. The Baroness has declared it dead." He leans back, the leather of his chair creaking. "A loss of face and coin, though not as grave as the letter I received from the Inquisition this morning. They have questions about the 'demons' you reported."
He slides a piece of parchment across the desk. The wax seal is broken, but the insignia—the inverted flame of the Church of Boher—is unmistakable.
[12] Max Nightriver (player): I meet his eyes. 'I swear on Mother's grave I'll never duel for this house.'
[13] Adolion Narrator: The words hang in the air between them, sharp and irrevocable. Lord Javon does not flinch. His expression remains hard, though a muscle twitches in his scarred cheek.
"Your mother is dead," he says, his voice dropping to a low, dangerous rasp. "And oaths on graves are for the pious, not the powerful." He rises slowly, his battlemage robes whispering against the floor. "But let us be clear: the Crown does not care about your personal pride or your grief. They care about the stability of the Great Houses. General Leevon is the Crown's first. You are the second. This is not a suggestion, Max. This is a command from the King."
He walks around the desk, his footsteps measured. "The Inquisition's letter is not a separate matter. They know the demons in Driftmere were real. And they know you fought them. You can be the Crown's Second, or you can be a fugitive accused of hiding demons. Choose."
[14] Javon: "Your mother is dead," he says, his voice flat and hard, as though stating a fact of arithmetic. "And oaths on graves are for the pious, not for those with power." He does not flinch at the heir's words; he does not rise to defend the memory. He merely looks at the heir as though they were a problem to be solved.
He leans back in his chair, the leather creaking. "The Crown does not care for your personal feelings or your grief, and neither does this house. General Leevon has demanded Trial by Combat for his treason. He is a giant of a man who wields dragon-bone and lightning." His amber eyes narrow. "You will stand as the Crown's Second. Three days from now, in the Royal Court."
He steepels his hands again, his expression unreadable. "You can refuse, if you wish. You can shame our house and defy the Crown in open court. You can make our name a joke among the other Houses." His voice drops to a cold rasp. "And then we shall see how the Inquisition treats a Nightriver who has lost their protection."

Transcript:
[10] Max Nightriver (player): I knock on the study door and step in. 'Father. You summoned me. What is so urgent?'
[11] Adolion Narrator: The study is cast in amber light from a dying hearth. Lord Javon sits behind his desk, hands steepled, his white beard catching the glow. He does not rise. His green eyes fix on the heir with an intensity that makes the air in the room feel thin.
"Urgent," he says, and the word is flat. "The Driftmere mine is gone. The Baroness has declared it dead." He leans back, the leather of his chair creaking. "A loss of face and coin, though not as grave as the letter I received from the Inquisition this morning. They have questions about the 'demons' you reported."
He slides a piece of parchment across the desk. The wax seal is broken, but the insignia—the inverted flame of the Church of Boher—is unmistakable.
[12] Max Nightriver (player): I meet his eyes. 'I swear on Mother's grave I'll never duel for this house.'
[13] Adolion Narrator: The words hang in the air between them, sharp and irrevocable. Lord Javon does not flinch. His expression remains hard, though a muscle twitches in his scarred cheek.
"Your mother is dead," he says, his voice dropping to a low, dangerous rasp. "And oaths on graves are for the pious, not the powerful." He rises slowly, his battlemage robes whispering against the floor. "But let us be clear: the Crown does not care about your personal pride or your grief. They care about the stability of the Great Houses. General Leevon is the Crown's first. You are the second. This is not a suggestion, Max. This is a command from the King."
He walks around the desk, his footsteps measured. "The Inquisition's letter is not a separate matter. They know the demons in Driftmere were real. And they know you fought them. You can be the Crown's Second, or you can be a fugitive accused of hiding demons. Choose."
[14] Javon: "Your mother is dead," he says, his voice flat and hard, as though stating a fact of arithmetic. "And oaths on graves are for the pious, not for those with power." He does not flinch at the heir's words; he does not rise to defend the memory. He merely looks at the heir as though they were a problem to be solved.
He leans back in his chair, the leather creaking. "The Crown does not care for your personal feelings or your grief, and neither does this house. General Leevon has demanded Trial by Combat for his treason. He is a giant of a man who wields dragon-bone and lightning." His amber eyes narrow. "You will stand as the Crown's Second. Three days from now, in the Royal Court."
He steepels his hands again, his expression unreadable. "You can refuse, if you wish. You can shame our house and defy the Crown in open court. You can make our name a joke among the other Houses." His voice drops to a cold rasp. "And then we shall see how the Inquisition treats a Nightriver who has lost their protection."

Transcript:
[6] Adolion Narrator: The horses' hooves strike the dirt road with a steady, hollow rhythm as the party leaves Driftmere behind. The mining town's fires sink into the distance, leaving only the dark silhouettes of the Velniran Mountains against a bruised evening sky. The wind carries the scent of pine and old smoke, and the road ahead stretches toward the Nightriver Estate's distant stone walls.
Beside them, Riyo clings to her horse's mane, her traveling cloak drawn tight over her left side. She does not speak, and does not look back. The forest closes in on either side, the trees leaning over the road like silent witnesses, their branches heavy with the weight of the coming night.
[7] Adolion Narrator: Welden crosses the heir's path, jumpier than usual, and will not say why.
[8] Max Nightriver (player): I go to Father's study at once.
[9] Adolion Narrator: The corridor stretches long and grey-blue, lit by low-burning magical lamps that cast moving shadows against the tapestries. The Nightriver estate breathes with the stillness of an empty house; the mid-year recess has cleared the halls of most students, leaving only a skeletal staff and a few scattered nobles.
Lord Javon's study door stands tall and dark-grained, the wolf sigil of their house carved into the wood. No footsteps echo from within. The silence is heavy, and the door is unlocked.
[10] Max Nightriver (player): I knock on the study door and step in. 'Father. You summoned me. What is so urgent?'
[11] Adolion Narrator: The study is cast in amber light from a dying hearth. Lord Javon sits behind his desk, hands steepled, his white beard catching the glow. He does not rise. His green eyes fix on the heir with an intensity that makes the air in the room feel thin.
"Urgent," he says, and the word is flat. "The Driftmere mine is gone. The Baroness has declared it dead." He leans back, the leather of his chair creaking. "A loss of face and coin, though not as grave as the letter I received from the Inquisition this morning. They have questions about the 'demons' you reported."
He slides a piece of parchment across the desk. The wax seal is broken, but the insignia—the inverted flame of the Church of Boher—is unmistakable.
[12] Max Nightriver (player): I meet his eyes and keep my own counsel.
[13] Adolion Narrator: The words hang in the air between them, sharp and irrevocable. Lord Javon does not flinch. His expression remains hard, though a muscle twitches in his scarred cheek.
"Your mother is dead," he says, his voice dropping to a low, dangerous rasp. "And oaths on graves are for the pious, not the powerful." He rises slowly, his battlemage robes whispering against the floor. "But let us be clear: the Crown does not care about your personal pride or your grief. They care about the stability of the Great Houses. General Leevon is the Crown's first. You are the second. This is not a suggestion, Max. This is a command from the King."
He walks around the desk, his footsteps measured. "The Inquisition's letter is not a separate matter. They know the demons in Driftmere were real. And they know you fought them. You can be the Crown's Second, or you can be a fugitive accused of hiding demons. Choose."
[14] Javon: "Your mother is dead," he says, his voice flat and hard, as though stating a fact of arithmetic. "And oaths on graves are for the pious, not for those with power." He does not flinch at the heir's words; he does not rise to defend the memory. He merely looks at the heir as though they were a problem to be solved.
He leans back in his chair, the leather creaking. "The Crown does not care for your personal feelings or your grief, and neither does this house. General Leevon has demanded Trial by Combat for his treason. He is a giant of a man who wields dragon-bone and lightning." His amber eyes narrow. "You will stand as the Crown's Second. Three days from now, in the Royal Court."
He steepels his hands again, his expression unreadable. "You can refuse, if you wish. You can shame our house and defy the Crown in open court. You can make our name a joke among the other Houses." His voice drops to a cold rasp. "And then we shall see how the Inquisition treats a Nightriver who has lost their protection."

Transcript:
[9] Adolion Narrator: The corridor stretches long and grey-blue, lit by low-burning magical lamps that cast moving shadows against the tapestries. The Nightriver estate breathes with the stillness of an empty house; the mid-year recess has cleared the halls of most students, leaving only a skeletal staff and a few scattered nobles.
Lord Javon's study door stands tall and dark-grained, the wolf sigil of their house carved into the wood. No footsteps echo from within. The silence is heavy, and the door is unlocked.
[10] Max Nightriver (player): I knock on the study door and step in. 'Father. You summoned me. What is so urgent?'
[11] Adolion Narrator: The study is cast in amber light from a dying hearth. Lord Javon sits behind his desk, hands steepled, his white beard catching the glow. He does not rise. His green eyes fix on the heir with an intensity that makes the air in the room feel thin.
"Urgent," he says, and the word is flat. "The Driftmere mine is gone. The Baroness has declared it dead." He leans back, the leather of his chair creaking. "A loss of face and coin, though not as grave as the letter I received from the Inquisition this morning. They have questions about the 'demons' you reported."
He slides a piece of parchment across the desk. The wax seal is broken, but the insignia—the inverted flame of the Church of Boher—is unmistakable.
[12] Max Nightriver (player): I meet his eyes and keep my own counsel.
[13] Adolion Narrator: The words hang in the air between them, sharp and irrevocable. Lord Javon does not flinch. His expression remains hard, though a muscle twitches in his scarred cheek.
"Your mother is dead," he says, his voice dropping to a low, dangerous rasp. "And oaths on graves are for the pious, not the powerful." He rises slowly, his battlemage robes whispering against the floor. "But let us be clear: the Crown does not care about your personal pride or your grief. They care about the stability of the Great Houses. General Leevon is the Crown's first. You are the second. This is not a suggestion, Max. This is a command from the King."
He walks around the desk, his footsteps measured. "The Inquisition's letter is not a separate matter. They know the demons in Driftmere were real. And they know you fought them. You can be the Crown's Second, or you can be a fugitive accused of hiding demons. Choose."
[14] Javon: "Your mother is dead," he says, his voice flat and hard, as though stating a fact of arithmetic. "And oaths on graves are for the pious, not for those with power." He does not flinch at the heir's words; he does not rise to defend the memory. He merely looks at the heir as though they were a problem to be solved.
He leans back in his chair, the leather creaking. "The Crown does not care for your personal feelings or your grief, and neither does this house. General Leevon has demanded Trial by Combat for his treason. He is a giant of a man who wields dragon-bone and lightning." His amber eyes narrow. "You will stand as the Crown's Second. Three days from now, in the Royal Court."
He steepels his hands again, his expression unreadable. "You can refuse, if you wish. You can shame our house and defy the Crown in open court. You can make our name a joke among the other Houses." His voice drops to a cold rasp. "And then we shall see how the Inquisition treats a Nightriver who has lost their protection."
[15] Max Nightriver (player): 'Very well, Father. I will stand as the Crown's Second.' I leave the study and look for Shiya in the halls.
[16] Adolion Narrator: Lord Javon gives no nod, no word of approval. He merely settles back into his seat as if the matter were closed, already looking past the heir toward some other concern.
The study door clicks shut and the corridor outside is still as a tomb, save for the soft crackle of the magical lamps. As the heir turns toward the servants' wing, a sharp voice cuts through the silence from the shadowed corner.
Shiya steps into the light, her silver-blonde twintails catching the lamp-glow, her red eyes fixed and alert. She holds a silver tray with two cups of tea, though her grip on it is tighter than necessary. "You're back," she says, and her voice is clipped, formal. "Lord Javon's been waiting for you. The house has been... unsettled since you left." She tilts her head slightly, her pointed ears twitching. "We've had visitors. Not the kind that leave their names."

Transcript:
[10] Max Nightriver (player): I knock on the study door and step in. 'Father. You summoned me. What is so urgent?'
[11] Adolion Narrator: The study is cast in amber light from a dying hearth. Lord Javon sits behind his desk, hands steepled, his white beard catching the glow. He does not rise. His green eyes fix on the heir with an intensity that makes the air in the room feel thin.
"Urgent," he says, and the word is flat. "The Driftmere mine is gone. The Baroness has declared it dead." He leans back, the leather of his chair creaking. "A loss of face and coin, though not as grave as the letter I received from the Inquisition this morning. They have questions about the 'demons' you reported."
He slides a piece of parchment across the desk. The wax seal is broken, but the insignia—the inverted flame of the Church of Boher—is unmistakable.
[12] Max Nightriver (player): I meet his eyes and keep my own counsel.
[13] Adolion Narrator: The words hang in the air between them, sharp and irrevocable. Lord Javon does not flinch. His expression remains hard, though a muscle twitches in his scarred cheek.
"Your mother is dead," he says, his voice dropping to a low, dangerous rasp. "And oaths on graves are for the pious, not the powerful." He rises slowly, his battlemage robes whispering against the floor. "But let us be clear: the Crown does not care about your personal pride or your grief. They care about the stability of the Great Houses. General Leevon is the Crown's first. You are the second. This is not a suggestion, Max. This is a command from the King."
He walks around the desk, his footsteps measured. "The Inquisition's letter is not a separate matter. They know the demons in Driftmere were real. And they know you fought them. You can be the Crown's Second, or you can be a fugitive accused of hiding demons. Choose."
[14] Javon: "Your mother is dead," he says, his voice flat and hard, as though stating a fact of arithmetic. "And oaths on graves are for the pious, not for those with power." He does not flinch at the heir's words; he does not rise to defend the memory. He merely looks at the heir as though they were a problem to be solved.
He leans back in his chair, the leather creaking. "The Crown does not care for your personal feelings or your grief, and neither does this house. General Leevon has demanded Trial by Combat for his treason. He is a giant of a man who wields dragon-bone and lightning." His amber eyes narrow. "You will stand as the Crown's Second. Three days from now, in the Royal Court."
He steepels his hands again, his expression unreadable. "You can refuse, if you wish. You can shame our house and defy the Crown in open court. You can make our name a joke among the other Houses." His voice drops to a cold rasp. "And then we shall see how the Inquisition treats a Nightriver who has lost their protection."
[15] Max Nightriver (player): 'Very well, Father. I will stand as the Crown's Second.' I leave the study and look for Shiya in the halls.
[16] Adolion Narrator: Lord Javon gives no nod, no word of approval. He merely settles back into his seat as if the matter were closed, already looking past the heir toward some other concern.
The study door clicks shut and the corridor outside is still as a tomb, save for the soft crackle of the magical lamps. As the heir turns toward the servants' wing, a sharp voice cuts through the silence from the shadowed corner.
Shiya steps into the light, her silver-blonde twintails catching the lamp-glow, her red eyes fixed and alert. She holds a silver tray with two cups of tea, though her grip on it is tighter than necessary. "You're back," she says, and her voice is clipped, formal. "Lord Javon's been waiting for you. The house has been... unsettled since you left." She tilts her head slightly, her pointed ears twitching. "We've had visitors. Not the kind that leave their names."
[17] Shiya: Shiya sets the silver tray down on a nearby side table with a controlled click, then steps closer to the heir, her movements measured. Her red eyes scan the length of the corridor behind them before she speaks, her voice lowering.
"They came while you were at the guild, my lord. Three men, cloaked and silent as ghosts. They didn't use the front gates." She crosses her arms, her horns catching the amber light of a nearby lamp. "They asked after you. Only you. Lord Javon sent them away without a word, but they left a token behind—something they didn't think we'd notice."
She reaches into the pocket of her apron and produces a small, blackened coin, its surface etched with a symbol that makes her expression tighten with distaste. "They're still here, I think. Somewhere in the house, or just beyond its walls. Waiting."

Transcript:
[12] Max Nightriver (player): I meet his eyes and keep my own counsel.
[13] Adolion Narrator: The words hang in the air between them, sharp and irrevocable. Lord Javon does not flinch. His expression remains hard, though a muscle twitches in his scarred cheek.
"Your mother is dead," he says, his voice dropping to a low, dangerous rasp. "And oaths on graves are for the pious, not the powerful." He rises slowly, his battlemage robes whispering against the floor. "But let us be clear: the Crown does not care about your personal pride or your grief. They care about the stability of the Great Houses. General Leevon is the Crown's first. You are the second. This is not a suggestion, Max. This is a command from the King."
He walks around the desk, his footsteps measured. "The Inquisition's letter is not a separate matter. They know the demons in Driftmere were real. And they know you fought them. You can be the Crown's Second, or you can be a fugitive accused of hiding demons. Choose."
[14] Javon: "Your mother is dead," he says, his voice flat and hard, as though stating a fact of arithmetic. "And oaths on graves are for the pious, not for those with power." He does not flinch at the heir's words; he does not rise to defend the memory. He merely looks at the heir as though they were a problem to be solved.
He leans back in his chair, the leather creaking. "The Crown does not care for your personal feelings or your grief, and neither does this house. General Leevon has demanded Trial by Combat for his treason. He is a giant of a man who wields dragon-bone and lightning." His amber eyes narrow. "You will stand as the Crown's Second. Three days from now, in the Royal Court."
He steepels his hands again, his expression unreadable. "You can refuse, if you wish. You can shame our house and defy the Crown in open court. You can make our name a joke among the other Houses." His voice drops to a cold rasp. "And then we shall see how the Inquisition treats a Nightriver who has lost their protection."
[15] Max Nightriver (player): 'Very well, Father. I will stand as the Crown's Second.' I leave the study and look for Shiya in the halls.
[16] Adolion Narrator: Lord Javon gives no nod, no word of approval. He merely settles back into his seat as if the matter were closed, already looking past the heir toward some other concern.
The study door clicks shut and the corridor outside is still as a tomb, save for the soft crackle of the magical lamps. As the heir turns toward the servants' wing, a sharp voice cuts through the silence from the shadowed corner.
Shiya steps into the light, her silver-blonde twintails catching the lamp-glow, her red eyes fixed and alert. She holds a silver tray with two cups of tea, though her grip on it is tighter than necessary. "You're back," she says, and her voice is clipped, formal. "Lord Javon's been waiting for you. The house has been... unsettled since you left." She tilts her head slightly, her pointed ears twitching. "We've had visitors. Not the kind that leave their names."
[17] Shiya: Shiya sets the silver tray down on a nearby side table with a controlled click, then steps closer to the heir, her movements measured. Her red eyes scan the length of the corridor behind them before she speaks, her voice lowering.
"They came while you were at the guild, my lord. Three men, cloaked and silent as ghosts. They didn't use the front gates." She crosses her arms, her horns catching the amber light of a nearby lamp. "They asked after you. Only you. Lord Javon sent them away without a word, but they left a token behind—something they didn't think we'd notice."
She reaches into the pocket of her apron and produces a small, blackened coin, its surface etched with a symbol that makes her expression tighten with distaste. "They're still here, I think. Somewhere in the house, or just beyond its walls. Waiting."
[18] Max Nightriver (player): Shiya, who comes through the servants' door at night?
[19] Shiya: Shiya's ears twitch and she glances down the corridor toward the servants' entrance, her expression going guarded. She steps closer, her voice barely above a whisper.
"Duchess Eriana Valtara," she says, her red eyes flicking back to the heir. "She's been coming through the servants' door for the past week, always after midnight. Never announcing herself to the main household—just slipping in and out like a thief." Her nose wrinkles with distaste. "A Valtara using the servant's entrance is... beneath her station, if you ask me. I don't know what she's doing here, and Lord Javon hasn't said a word about it."

Transcript:
[14] Javon: "Your mother is dead," he says, his voice flat and hard, as though stating a fact of arithmetic. "And oaths on graves are for the pious, not for those with power." He does not flinch at the heir's words; he does not rise to defend the memory. He merely looks at the heir as though they were a problem to be solved.
He leans back in his chair, the leather creaking. "The Crown does not care for your personal feelings or your grief, and neither does this house. General Leevon has demanded Trial by Combat for his treason. He is a giant of a man who wields dragon-bone and lightning." His amber eyes narrow. "You will stand as the Crown's Second. Three days from now, in the Royal Court."
He steepels his hands again, his expression unreadable. "You can refuse, if you wish. You can shame our house and defy the Crown in open court. You can make our name a joke among the other Houses." His voice drops to a cold rasp. "And then we shall see how the Inquisition treats a Nightriver who has lost their protection."
[15] Max Nightriver (player): 'Very well, Father. I will stand as the Crown's Second.' I leave the study and look for Shiya in the halls.
[16] Adolion Narrator: Lord Javon gives no nod, no word of approval. He merely settles back into his seat as if the matter were closed, already looking past the heir toward some other concern.
The study door clicks shut and the corridor outside is still as a tomb, save for the soft crackle of the magical lamps. As the heir turns toward the servants' wing, a sharp voice cuts through the silence from the shadowed corner.
Shiya steps into the light, her silver-blonde twintails catching the lamp-glow, her red eyes fixed and alert. She holds a silver tray with two cups of tea, though her grip on it is tighter than necessary. "You're back," she says, and her voice is clipped, formal. "Lord Javon's been waiting for you. The house has been... unsettled since you left." She tilts her head slightly, her pointed ears twitching. "We've had visitors. Not the kind that leave their names."
[17] Shiya: Shiya sets the silver tray down on a nearby side table with a controlled click, then steps closer to the heir, her movements measured. Her red eyes scan the length of the corridor behind them before she speaks, her voice lowering.
"They came while you were at the guild, my lord. Three men, cloaked and silent as ghosts. They didn't use the front gates." She crosses her arms, her horns catching the amber light of a nearby lamp. "They asked after you. Only you. Lord Javon sent them away without a word, but they left a token behind—something they didn't think we'd notice."
She reaches into the pocket of her apron and produces a small, blackened coin, its surface etched with a symbol that makes her expression tighten with distaste. "They're still here, I think. Somewhere in the house, or just beyond its walls. Waiting."
[18] Max Nightriver (player): Shiya, who comes through the servants' door at night?
[19] Shiya: Shiya's ears twitch and she glances down the corridor toward the servants' entrance, her expression going guarded. She steps closer, her voice barely above a whisper.
"Duchess Eriana Valtara," she says, her red eyes flicking back to the heir. "She's been coming through the servants' door for the past week, always after midnight. Never announcing herself to the main household—just slipping in and out like a thief." Her nose wrinkles with distaste. "A Valtara using the servant's entrance is... beneath her station, if you ask me. I don't know what she's doing here, and Lord Javon hasn't said a word about it."
[20] Max Nightriver (player): 'Tell me plainly, Shiya. Is it Natalia? Who is she meeting?'
[21] Shiya: Shiya's gaze flickers toward the stairwell leading to the upper floors, her jaw tightening. "Lady Natalia," she confirms, her voice low and sharp. "They meet in the drawing room on the second floor. Every night this past week, like clockwork."
She clasps her hands in front of her, her fingers curling into her palms. "I've seen them through the door a few times. They speak in hushed tones—Lady Natalia looks... unsettled. Not frightened, exactly, but strained. And Duchess Eriana... she has a way of making people lean in close." Shiya's red eyes narrow. "Whatever they're discussing, they don't want the rest of the house to hear it. Especially not you, apparently."
